question:
The father is himself being held captive by a kidnapper, and the kidnapper is on the phone with the father's daughter—who is elsewhere and safe—demanding that she bring one hundred million yen alone by noon with no police, or the father (the hostage) will be killed. The father, held near the kidnapper, hears the call, including his daughter begging for his life to be spared.

The father decides the ransom should not be paid because paying it cannot save him—he believes the kidnapper will kill him regardless of whether the money is delivered—while it would gravely endanger his daughter. She would have to gather and bring the money alone with no police, meaning no witnesses, and once she had delivered it and could identify the kidnapper, she would be killed as a witness. He also sees that "alone, no police" is exactly the trap that removes any protection.

So paying guarantees nothing for him and would draw his daughter into mortal danger. He therefore tells her not to pay or come, sacrificing his own life to keep her away and safe.

The father is himself the kidnapped hostage—physically held, with his life genuinely at stake. The kidnapper is on the phone with the father's daughter, who is safe, free, and elsewhere, and demands that she bring one hundred million yen alone by noon the next day with no police, or the father will be killed. The daughter, believing her father is in danger, begs over the phone for his life to be spared. The father hears the whole call because he is being held near the kidnapper.

The father concludes that the ransom should not be paid because, in his judgment, paying cannot save him while it would destroy his daughter. He does not expect to be released or rescued and accepts that his own life is lost regardless. But he realizes the demand—come alone, bring the money, tell no police—is a trap: if his daughter obeys, the kidnapper will take the money and then kill both of them to eliminate witnesses, so she would be murdered. If she stays away, she remains safe and survives.

Therefore the only thing paying the ransom would accomplish is to draw his daughter into the trap and get her killed. He decides the ransom must not be paid and tells her not to pay or come, sacrificing his own life to keep her away and safe.
